newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 2.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HUGE PAY-OUT TO SACKED BANKER

An industrial tribunal has ruled that Goldman Sachs, the US investment bank, discriminated against a black American bond salesman employed in its London offices. The ruling that James Curry suffered racial discrimination and unfair dismissal could leave Goldman Sachs having to pay hundreds of thousands of pounds in compensation. The bank had strongly denied the allegations, and reiterated after the ruling that it did 'not discriminate'.
-- MENZIES HAS CLEAR-OUT AT EARLY LEARNING

Retailer John Menzies has decided to replace the senior management team at Early Learning Centres, its troubled chain of children's shops. The move comes after a disappointing trade performance at the chain, and head-hunters have been appointed to seek a new chief executive. Menzies issued a profits warning in January, citing a slump in Christmas toy sales at Early Learning Centre.
-- LEHMAN BUYS STAKE IN ACORN

US investment house Lehman Brothers has paid Italy's Olivetti 23.2 million stg to acquire a 14.7 percent stake in Acorn, the UK-based electronics company. Lehman will place the shares with institutional investors over the next couple of months, although it has also arranged a complex derivative contract with Olivetti as protection. Cambridge-based Acorn was rescued by Olivetti after running into problems making BBC computers.
THE TIMES
-- BUDGET HOPES SEND SHARE INDEX SOARING

Shares on the London Stock Exchange soared on Tuesday in a wave of pre-budget optimism. The FT-SE 100 index of leading stocks rose 123.7 points to close at 4783.3, just short of the market's all-time high, which was set last month. Tuesday's surge came as dealers predicted that Chancellor Gordon Brown would hit consumers, particularly home-owners, with tax increases of up to five billion stg. Such a move would help calm the economy and reduce the need for further rises in interest rates.
-- AMERSHAM PROPOSES 2 BILLION STG BIOTECH MERGER

Health care company Amersham International has announced a 2.1-billion-stg deal to combine its diagnostic imaging agents business with Nycomed of Norway. The move is the second major deal involving Amersham and a Scandinavian company, coming just weeks after the merger with Sweden's Pharmacia Biotech. Amersham said the Nycomed merger would make it the world leader in diagnostic imaging agents.
-- FLEXTECH CHIEF IN 4.3 MILLION STG SHARE SALE

The chief executive of Flextech, the supplier of cable and satellite programming, has sold most of his shares in the company to US media firm Tele-Communications International. The sale of the almost 700,000 shares will earn Roger Luard about 4.3 million stg and, along with the purchase of another 50,000 shares from Flextech finance director Mark Luiz, gives TCI a 36.3 percent interest in the company.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LONDON AND PARIS THROW EUROTUNNEL A LIFELINE

Britain and France have agreed on an extension of Eurotunnel's licence to at least 2086, provided shareholders support the company's 8.5 million stg restructuring plan. The governments have requested a share of the company's profits and want Eurotunnel officials to look into methods of increasing freight traffic through the tunnel and beyond. Provided shareholders continue receive an 'adequate return', and that no such payments are levied until after 2052, when the existing licence would have ended, Eurotunnel will agree to the arrangements.
-- C&W USES AUSTRALIA TO TIGHTEN GRIP ON PACIFIC RIM

Cable & Wireless, the second largest telecommunications operator in the UK, has revealed it will strengthen its shares in Australian telecoms operator Optus through the purchase of a 24.5 percent stake in the group for 445 million stg. The deal would give C&W 49 percent of the company and the option to buy additional stakes. C&W, meanwhile, is to cut its shares in China Telecom by 5.5 percent and is seeking to pull out of Columbia's open market telephone company, NEC.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SMITH WARNS ITV'S REGIONAL DIFFERENCES MUST STAY

Heritage Secretary Chris Smith has said that the regional identity of Britain's ITV companies must be kept intact despite the current consolidation in the industry. Speaking at a conference on the future of UK broadcasting, Smith also dismissed as unlikely a recent prediction by Gerry Robinson, chairman of Granada Group, that all the ITV stations would merge within a decade.
-- ARNAULT SET TO TALK WITH SPIRITS GROUPS

Bernard Arnault, head of French luxury goods group LVMH, which has been trying to block the proposed mega-merger of drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, is due to talk to the two groups on Wednesday afternoon. However, the negotiations appear doomed to failure unless one side is prepared to make a last-minute concession. It is understood that LVMH would reject a rumoured offer from Guinness and GrandMet to give Arnault an equity stake in the combined spirits division of the merged group.
-- ORANGE TOPS MOBILE PHONE GROWTH TABLE

Figures released Tuesday show that market leader Orange maintained its lead amid stiff competition for mobile telephone customers in the spring. Of the four major UK mobile networks, Vodafone's net UK subscriber base grew by just 53,000 between April and June to 2.9 million, placing it fourth in terms of growth. Orange saw its share increase by 86,000, to 980,000, placing the company on top of the growth table for the second quarter in a row.
